subject: Startups
title: SAFEs and Convertible Notes
description: A fast breakdown of SAFEs and Convertible Notes for builders.

hook.text: You need money but can't agree on a valuation. A SAFE lets you take the cash now and price the equity later.

buildup.text: Y Combinator created the SAFE—Simple Agreement for Future Equity—to simplify early-stage fundraising.

discovery.text: A SAFE converts to equity at the next priced round, usually with a valuation cap that rewards early investors.

twist.text: SAFEs aren't debt—no interest, no maturity date. Convertible notes are debt and accrue interest until they convert.

climax.text: SAFEs are founder-friendly: simpler, cheaper, faster.

punchline.text: SAFEs delay the valuation debate. But the bill comes due later.

quiz.question: What is a SAFE?
options: A Simple Agreement for Future Equity
